Problem 4 Titrimetric Analysis of Etching Acids
Wet chemical etching is a major process in the semiconductor-chip industry. It uses acidic substances to corrode a substrate surface and thereby achieve etching. A mixture of hydrofluoric acid, fluorosilicic acid, and nitric acid is a common etchant. A rapid and accurate laboratory method for determining the contents of these three acids in an etchant is described below.

subquestions.text_open:
Procedure background: Accurately weigh 3.028 g of the sample. Place 1.502 g of it in a plastic beaker to prepare test solution A, and use the remaining sample to prepare test solution B by the same procedure. During preparation, add 10 mL of saturated $KNO_3$ solution and anhydrous ethanol, mix, dilute with anhydrous ethanol, and let stand for approximately 20 min until the precipitate has completely settled into a separate layer. Label this as test solution A. Prepare test solution B from the remaining sample by the same procedure.
4.1.2 State the purpose of adding saturated KNO_3 solution.

4.2 Titrimetric analysis. Add 30 mL of water and 3 drops of phenolphthalein indicator to test solution A. Titrate with 0.5018 $\mathrm{mol \cdot L^{-1}}$ standard NaOH solution until the solution becomes faint pink; 24.39 mL of the standard NaOH solution is consumed. Add 30 mL of water and 2 drops of methyl-orange indicator to test solution B. Adjust the pH with NaOH solution until the solution just turns bright yellow. Using a fluoride-ion combination electrode as the measuring electrode, titrate with 0.08273 $\mathrm{mol \cdot L^{-1}}$ standard La(NO_3)_3 solution; precipitate forms continuously during the titration. At the endpoint, 25.11 mL of La(NO_3)_3 solution is consumed. Weigh 0.5003 g of the original sample into a beaker containing 15 mL of 0.5 $\mathrm{mol \cdot L^{-1}}$ NaOH solution, add water to 60 mL, and verify with pH paper that the pH is greater than 13. Heat slowly to boiling, maintain a gentle boil for 5 min, and cool to room temperature. Add 2 drops of methyl-red indicator, adjust with nitric acid until red, and then adjust with NaOH solution until the solution just turns bright yellow. Using a fluoride-ion combination electrode as the indicator electrode, titrate with 0.08273 $\mathrm{mol \cdot L^{-1}}$ standard La(NO_3)_3 solution. At the endpoint, 15.28 mL is consumed. 4.2.1 Write all reaction equations occurring in Sections 4.1 and 4.2; write repeated reactions only once.
4.2.2 Calculate the mass fractions of HF, H_2SiF_6, and HNO_3 in the sample. Note: the fluoride-ion electrode indicates the endpoint by the abrupt change in fluoride-ion concentration.
